items.title: Aynı Yasal Duyuru, Aynı Değişim… Yoksa Değil mi?
items.author: hanyzanaty
items.text:
The Question 
 Open the roadmap. It looks familiar. 
 Open the H1 2027 Türkiye Payroll roadmap and the first impression is familiar. 
 Five Legal Changes. 
 New rules. 
 New dates. 
 New payroll work. 
 The normal question is obvious: 
 What do we need to change to stay compliant? 
 For TR00, the established payroll schema, that often means checking what is already supported, updating statutory parameters or enhancing existing logic where required, and keeping the solution aligned with applicable legislation. 
 Ama… 
 with TR01, our newer payroll schema, there is another question worth asking. Can we respond to the legal change without creating the next special case? 
 And sometimes there is an even more important question: Should we build something new at all? 
 That changes how I read this roadmap. Not as five identical development commitments, but as five opportunities to make a deliberate product decision. 
 ....... 
 TR01 is not about redesigning everything every time a new law arrives. 
 Compliance matters. Her zaman. But the best product response is not always a new payroll function or a new configuration table. 
 Sometimes we reuse something proven. Sometimes we automate manual administration. Sometimes a statutory scenario helps shape a reusable framework. And sometimes, after listening to the market, we decide that an implementation is not a priority for the current roadmap. 
 Some enhancements also began with our implementation partners, independently of any particular legal announcement. The legal changes give us a way to test whether those ideas can serve more than one scenario. 
 Here is how those decisions appear across the five roadmap topics, ordered by their current request delivery targets. 
 ....... 
 Five Legal Changes, Five Product Decisions 
 The laws differ. So do the solutions. 
 Nitelikli Hizmet Merkezi Gelir Vergisi ve Damga Vergisi İstisnası 
 First, Qualified Service Centers. 
 The legal change provides an Income Tax and Stamp Tax exemption on qualifying remuneration for eligible personnel, up to a statutory ceiling: three times the gross minimum wage for standard centers and five times for eligible special locations. The amount above the ceiling remains taxable. SGK contributions are not changed by this specific exemption. 
 For TR00 , we have not identified a relevant customer population. Consequently, a TR00 implementation is not planned in the current delivery scope . The legal obligation itself does not disappear for employers to whom it applies. 
 For TR01 , the more valuable direction is not another hard-coded exception for one type of employer. 
 Instead, we plan a Configurable Statutory Exemption Framework with two distinct approaches: one for exemptions applied to an eligible remuneration base, and another for exemptions on specific additional payments, allowances or benefits. 
 The design direction includes configurable wage-type eligibility, statutory percentages and ceilings, relevant employee or workplace conditions, and distinct SGK, Income Tax and Stamp Tax treatments. Existing net-to-gross processing should apply those results consistently rather than requiring a separate gross-up engine. 
 Qualified Service Center is the immediate legal scenario. The ambition is a framework that can support other statutory exemptions when their rules require it. 
 Yani… not every new exemption deserves its own permanent branch in payroll logic. 
 ....... 
 Kıdem Tazminatı Tavanı ve Vergiden Müstesna Çocuk Yardımı Tutarları 
 Next, child allowance. 
 For the second half of 2026, the Income Tax exemption thresholds for employer-paid child allowances are TRY 787.76 per child up to and including 72 months, and TRY 393.88 for children older than 72 months. Income Tax and SGK exemptions follow different statutory rules. 
 For TR00 , we can build on the existing child-allowance and SGK treatment. The planned work focuses on the age-band Income Tax exemption and on making the allowance easier to maintain: enter the amount per child and eligible child count, then let payroll calculate the total. 
 For TR01 , we can reduce a different manual step. 
 Instead of requiring HR to enter child counts repeatedly through age-band wage types, the planned enhancement reads IT0021 Family Members , determines eligible children and their age bands, and uses a configurable source for the employer-paid rate. 
 We are not introducing a separate SGK-to-Income-Tax-base configuration as part of this item. The objective is to automate the data that payroll already needs while preserving the established statutory calculations. 
 Less duplicate maintenance. More consistent eligibility data. 
 ....... 
 Uzaktan Çalışma Yönetmeliğinde Değişiklik Yapıldı 
 Then, remote work. 
 The September 2026 amendment strengthens contractual requirements for hybrid arrangements, including the distinction between on-site and remote working days and hours. Employers also need to report remote-working days correctly through the applicable e-declaration process. 
 Here, the lesson is that reuse can be better than reinnovation by invention . 
 For TR00 , reporting of remote-working days is already supported through the existing wage-type classification and e-declaration process, documented in SAP Note 3063529. The immediate task is to validate the customer configuration and the quantity passed to reporting, not to redesign SGK or Income Tax calculations. 
 For TR01 , the planned approach is to reuse that proven pattern: identify the relevant wage type through Evaluation Class 11, carry its remote-working-day quantity in payroll results, and report it using HTRCEDE0 . 
 We are not planning a new generic statutory day-count engine for this legal change. The source and treatment of partial remote-day quantities still need to follow confirmed legal rules and the appropriate existing configuration. 
 Sometimes the most scalable design decision is simply to avoid building something twice. 
 ....... 
 SGK Turizm Ücret Desteği Genelgesi Yayımlandı 
 Tourism Wage Support leads to a different decision. 
 This temporary measure covers the period from May to December 2026. It is an employer-side support ( destek ), not an employee SGK or Income Tax exemption. The statutory model uses eligible SGK premium days and a daily amount of TRY 116.67 , subject to the applicable employer-premium cap; SGK handles the official offset. 
 After considering partner feedback and identified customer demand, implementation of Tourism Wage Support is not planned for either TR00 or TR01 in the current scope . That is a product prioritization decision, not a change to employers' legal obligations. 
 Instead, we are prioritizing a separate TR01 enhancement that partners expect to deliver more everyday value: Recurring Meal Allowance . 
 Today, maintaining eligible meal days can involve repetitive entries and manual work when a daily rate changes during the month. 
 The planned TR01 enhancement uses a recurring IT0014 entry, derives eligible days from planned working days and applicable non-working-day information, and prorates the payment when the rate changes. It reuses existing SGK and Income Tax exemption processing rather than inventing new statutory meal rules. 
 One initiative is deliberately not being built now. Another, independent improvement is moving forward. 
 That is also a roadmap decision worth explaining. 
 ....... 
 2027 Asgari Ücret Tespit Komisyonu Kararı ve Gelir Vergisi Tarifesi 
 And finally, the annual cycle. 
 At the time of this draft, the official 2027 minimum-wage and Income Tax parameters have not yet been announced. Based on the usual cycle, SAP localization expects the relevant announcements toward the end of December 2026; actual values and effective dates remain subject to the authorities' publications. 
 For TR00 , the established priority is straightforward: update the relevant statutory parameters when confirmed, including the applicable severance ceiling on its own publication and effective-date schedule. 
 For TR01 , the annual update sits alongside a more substantial foundation initiative: bringing Severance/Indemnity calculations into the payroll schema . 
 The first planned phase covers core statutory severance and notice indemnity calculations, together with a separate monthly severance provision. For that provision, payroll evaluates accumulated service and the applicable full provision at month-end, then calculates the adjustment against the previous month's closing provision balance. 
 That provision is an accounting calculation, not an employee payment ; the precise financial and IFRS/TFRS treatment remains subject to validation. 
 More advanced termination settlement, off-cycle payment scenarios and annual leave provisioning or payout are possible future extensions, not part of the initial delivery commitment. 
 The opportunity is to establish a sound payroll foundation now without pretending that every related settlement scenario must be delivered at once. 
 ....... 
 Beyond Legal Changes — Improving the TR01 Foundation 
 But not every improvement needs a new law. 
 During our Türkiye Payroll partner roundtables, some of the most valuable feedback came from everyday implementation experience. 
 A deduction carried into the wrong payroll split after a company change. A configuration value that consultants must enter manually. An Excel export that removes leading zeros from statutory reporting fields. 
 Small details? 
 Perhaps. Until they affect payroll accuracy, require unnecessary workarounds, or interrupt statutory reporting. 
 That is why, alongside the five Legal Changes, we have also prioritized six TR01 corrections and usability improvements , targeting the end of November 2026. 
 They address three practical areas: 
 Payroll correctness: Improving carry-forward deduction handling, wage-type processing flexibility, and payroll schema execution. 
 Configuration usability: Making T7TR parameter maintenance easier through search help and IMG integration. 
 Reporting reliability: Preserving leading zeros in E-Declaration Excel exports to avoid invalid reporting files. 
 None of these requires a new statutory announcement. 
 They come directly from implementation partners working with TR01 and identifying where the solution can work better. 
 İşte bu. 
 Reinnovation is not only about introducing new capabilities. Sometimes it means fixing what gets in the way of using the capabilities we already have. 
 ....... 
 The Pattern 
 Put these decisions together and a different pattern emerges. 
 An established process → reuse and validate it before designing a replacement. 
 Repeated manual maintenance → derive information from existing employee or working-time data where appropriate. 
 A recurring statutory scenario → build a configurable framework when it creates genuine reuse. 
 Limited customer demand → make a transparent decision about what not to prioritize. 
 Everyday implementation friction → correct the foundation, even without a new law. 
 Three streams reinforce one another: statutory compliance, reusable product enhancements, and continuous improvement . 
 They do not always require the same technical response or the same delivery timeline. 
 ....... 
 The Design Principle 
 Each legal change invites a design decision — not necessarily new development. 
 TR01 is not simply TR00 rewritten. And it is not a redesign project hiding behind every legal change. 
 It is a habit of asking one extra question when change arrives: What is the simplest sustainable response — reuse, automation, configuration, a focused correction, or a conscious decision to defer? 
 Not every legal change will produce a reusable capability. Not every partner request will become a committed delivery. And not every proposed improvement needs a new engine. 
 But every decision should be clear about the customer problem it solves. 
 ....... 
 Haydi Konuşalım 
 The best product decisions begin with the right

items.title: Generative AI vs Agentic AI in SAP: Understanding the Difference
items.author: Myvizhipriya_Thangaraj_2810
items.text:
Overview: 
 When I started learning about Artificial Intelligence (AI), I kept thinking about one thing: How can AI actually help businesses in their day-to-day work, especially in systems like SAP? 
 We know SAP helps businesses manage different processes such as finance, procurement, sales, inventory and supply chain. But with AI becoming more common, I wanted to understand how it could make these processes easier, smarter and more efficient. 
 While exploring on this topic, I came across two termsinologies that caught my attention: Generative AI and Agentic AI. 
 To be honest, at first, I found them quite similar and I wasn’t sure what really made them different. So, I started exploring how each of them works and how they could be used in real SAP business scenarios. 
 In this blog, I’ll share what I’ve learned so far, explain the difference between Generative AI and Agentic AI in simple terms and walk through a few practical examples from the SAP world. 
 Let’s understand it step by step! 

 What Is Generative AI? 
 Creates content: Generative AI uses our instructions to generate text, explanations, code, and other content. 
 Helps with SAP tasks : It can explain SAP processes, draft functional specifications, help us understand ABAP code, and prepare test scenarios. 
 Needs verification: AI can make mistakes, so we should check its answers against our SAP system and business requirements. 
 How Does Generative AI Work? 
 Learns patterns: The AI model learns patterns from large amounts of training data. 
 Responds to prompts: We provide an instruction, and the model generates a response based on its training and available context. 
 Improves through follow-up prompts: We can ask for simpler explanations, examples, or summaries, but the results still need to be checked. 

 Picture 1: Generative AI vs Agentic AI 

 What Is Agentic AI? 
 Works toward a goal: Agentic AI can plan and coordinate multiple steps to solve a problem. 
 Uses connected tools: In SAP, an AI agent could check invoice details, compare purchase orders and goods receipts, and identify discrepancies. 
 Supports next steps: It can recommend actions or perform approved tasks, depending on its integrations and permissions. 
 How Does Agentic AI Work? 
 Understand and plan: Identify the goal and decide which steps are needed. 
 Act and verify: Use authorized tools to gather information, check results, and perform additional checks if necessary. 
 Respond or take action: Present the findings, recommend a solution, or initiate an approved action. 
 In simple terms: Generative AI helps us create answers; Agentic AI helps us work toward outcomes. 

 Generative AI vs Agentic AI: What Is the Difference? 
 Let's compare both concepts using following SAP examples. 

 Picture 2: Which AI approach fits in the Task 
 They are connected concepts, and an AI agent may use a generative model as one of its core capabilities. 
 Generative AI focuses on generating useful outputs, while Agentic AI focuses on coordinating actions toward a goal. 

 How Does This Relate to SAP Joule? 
 1. Meet SAP Joule: Joule is SAP’s AI copilot that brings AI assistance into supported SAP applications and workflows. 
 2. Ask in simple language: Users can ask questions naturally instead of navigating complex screens for every task, depending on the available features. 
 3. Understand business context: Joule can help users find information and understand business processes using relevant enterprise context and authorized data. 
 4. Go beyond answers: Supported AI agent capabilities can coordinate multiple steps across business processes and applications, depending on integrations and permissions. 
 5. Know the difference: Generative AI creates content, AI agents work toward goals using tools and actions, and Joule provides AI capabilities within SAP’s enterprise ecosystem. 
 The key takeaway: In SAP, AI is not just about getting answers. It’s about making business processes easier to understand, support and execute. 

 What Should SAP Professionals Keep in Mind? 
 As AI becomes more relevant to enterprise applications, I believe SAP professionals should keep a few important points in mind. 

 Picture 3: Key AI Considerations 
 For SAP consultants, developers, and business analysts, these considerations are just as important as understanding the technology itself. 

 Generative AI vs Agentic AI: Pros & Cons 
 Like any technology, AI has its own pros and cons. In SAP, it can save time, reduce repetitive work, and make it easier to understand business processes. But it can also give incorrect answers, raise data security concerns, and require extra effort to integrate with existing systems. So, while AI can make our work easier, we still need to use it carefully and apply our own judgment . 

 Picture 4: Generative AI vs Agentic AI: Pros & Cons 

 Final Thoughts 
 I believe the first step is not to ask whether Generative AI or Agentic AI is better. Instead, we should ask what business problem we want to solve, what data and tools are required, and how AI can help us achieve the desired outcome safely and effectively. 
 AI in SAP is not just about generating answers. It is about finding practical ways to connect intelligence with business processes, reduce repetitive work, and help people make better decisions. 
 And understanding the difference between Generative AI and Agentic AI is a useful starting point for exploring that opportunity. 
 Thank you for taking the time to read this blog! If you found this helpful, i would love to hear your thoughts, feedback or questions in the comments. Let's keep learning and growing together! 
 I’m still new to blogging, so if you notice anything that could be improved or corrected, please don’t hesitate to let me know!!

items.author: kavya_nimmagadda24
items.text:
The goal of this Integration is to ensure that users in SAP FSA to have the right permissions for access to business objects based on the organizational levels they are assigned in SAP S/4 HANA. Both Initial and Delta load are supported. 
 In the past we have supported only Legacy Org Integration to FSA and with this new Integration, we support Enterprise Service org Integration as well providing the flexibility to the customers to choose the right organizational model that is applicable for them. 
 There are two parts to this Integration:

items.title: Works Council Engagement: The Make-or-Break Step in M&A HR (HCM) System Migrations
items.author: manubhutani
items.text:
HR TECHNOLOGY M&A INTEGRATION 
 Works Council Engagement: The Make-or-Break Step in M&A HR System Migrations 
 Co-determination, consultation, and approval rights over HR systems and employee data 

 Who this is for: program leads, HRIS teams, Legal, and Privacy teams moving an acquired workforce onto a new HR platform (for example from Workday into SAP SuccessFactors) where acquired employees sit in countries with works councils. 
 1. Why this is a gating item? 
 Works council engagement is not a lift and shift vs. harmonize choice. In countries with works councils, the council often has legal rights to be informed, consulted, or to approve a new HR system before employee data can move. Missing this can delay go-live regardless of how ready the technology is. 

 The core message 
 A system can be fully configured, tested, and signed off by the business, and still be blocked at the last step. Treat works council approval as a formal go-live readiness criteria, owned and tracked like any other critical path item. 

 2. Understand the rights you are dealing with 
 The spectrum of works council rights 

 INFORM 
 → 
 CONSULT 
 → 
 CONSENT 

 Council receives the facts 
 before decisions are final 

 Council gives an opinion 
 and the employer must hear it 
 before deciding 

 No lawful rollout without 
 agreement, or a substitute 
 ruling or conciliation 
 Rights differ by country and by what the system does. Always confirm with local counsel. 
 Why HR systems usually trigger these rights? 
 An HR platform holds personnel data, and rules about processing and protecting that data are often subject to council rights. 
 Several statutes look at capability, not intent. A system that can observe or record behavior or performance can trigger consent rights even if the employer promises not to use it that way. 
 Talent modules go further. Performance, goals, and assessment criteria are frequently treated as evaluation schemes, which have their own consent or consultation rules. 
 Analytics, dashboards, and AI-assisted features can widen the scope. Switching a feature on later can reopen the discussion. 
 How the level shapes your plan? 

 Level 
 What it means for the program 
 Plan for 

 Inform 
 No veto, but early notice builds trust and avoids disputes later 
 • Brief the council early 
 • Share a dossier summary and a named contact 

 Consult 
 The council's opinion must be heard before the decision is taken, so timing matters 
 • Allow a real review period 
 • Document how feedback was handled 
 • Decide only after consultation closes 

 Consent 
 The council can withhold agreement, which may lead to negotiation, conciliation, or a court route 
 • Treat as critical path 
 • Negotiate a written agreement 
 • Prepare a contingency per country 

 3. What works councils typically focus on? 
 Councils generally ask the same core questions, even when the legal basis differs. Preparing a clear answer to each, in writing and in the local language, is the single most effective way to shorten the process. 

 Topic 
 What the council asks 
 What should be done 

 Data 
 What employee data is collected, what moves to the new system, and why it is needed 
 • Field-level data inventory: field, source, target, purpose 
 • Rationale for each category, and what is not migrated 

 Data security 
 Where data is hosted, how it is protected, and who else can touch it 
 • Hosting location, encryption, cross-border transfer mechanism 
 • Vendor and sub-processor list with access scope 

 Data access 
 Who can see what, and how sensitive fields are protected 
 • Role and permission matrix (managers, HR) 
 • Live demo of what each role sees, including sensitive fields 

 Historical data 
 What is retained, what is archived, and how people can reach their records 
 • Retention schedule and archive location 
 • Process for current and former employees to request records 

 Monitoring 
 Assurance that the system will not be used to watch individuals 
 • Written statement of purposes and prohibited uses 
 • Status of analytics and AI features (on, off, planned) 

 Language 
 Whether employees can understand and use the system 
 • Translated job aids, notices, and training 
 • Known language gaps and the mitigation 

 Employee rights 
 How access, correction, and deletion requests are handled 
 • GDPR rights process and contacts 
 • Employee notice and communication plan 

 Tip: share the data model, not the data 
 The inventory should describe data elements and purposes, not individual employee records. Disclosing personal data to the council can itself need a legal basis, so keep examples anonymized or in test data. 

 4. A practical engagement approach 
 Run the works council track as its own workstream with an owner, a plan, and a status line in the program dashboard. A five-phase approach keeps Legal, Privacy, HR, and the program team aligned. 
 Five phases of works council engagement 

 1 Scope 
 2 Prepare 
 3 Brief and demo 
 4 Agree 
 5 Sustain 

 • Identify entities and countries 
 • Confirm council exists and level (local or central) 
 • Agree owners and timeline 
 • Align Legal, Privacy, HR on one answer set 
 • Translate key materials 
 • Early briefing, before design is final 
 • Live demos of security and access 
 • Log questions and commitments 
 • Negotiate works agreement or opinion 
 • Resolve open points in writing 
 • Obtain formal approval or consultation close 
 • Track as go-live criteria 
 • Re-open if scope changes 
 • Keep a named contact post go-live 

 Best practices: 
 Engage early, before design is final. Councils want to shape decisions, not rubber-stamp them. 
 If time permits bring critical employee level attributes inventory showing what is migrated and why. 
 Run live demos of the actual security model, role access, and what managers can see. 
 Be consistent with all countries works council: Align Legal, Privacy, and local HR, and document commitments in a works agreement where required. 
 Plan for their cycle. Build review cycles (weeks to months) into the plan, provide translated materials and a named contact, and track approval as a formal go-live readiness criteria.

items.title: Must-Knows: Moving a Non-SAP Workforce to SuccessFactors in an M&A Engagement
items.author: manubhutani
items.text:
Must-Knows: Moving a Non-SAP Workforce to SuccessFactors in an M&A Engagement 
 Lift and shift or harmonize? A high-level guide to the critical focus areas 

 Applies when the parent runs on SAP SuccessFactors and acquired company runs on a different HR platform like Workday. 
 Summary 
 When an acquired company runs on a non-SAP HCM platform and the parent runs on SAP SuccessFactors, the integration is rarely a single decision. It is a series of area-by-area choices between two paths: lift and shift the acquired company's way of working or harmonize onto the parent's standards. 
 Two ways to bring an acquired population into the parent system 

 LIFT AND SHIFT 
 HARMONIZE 

 • Keep the acquired structures 
 • Fastest path and lowest Day 1 risk (based upon TSA timeline) 
 • Honors commitments to employees 
 • Creates clean-up work after go-live 
 • Adopt the parent's standards 
 • Unified structure, cleaner analytics 
 • Needs HR and business alignment 
 • Higher change impact for employees on day 1 

 Part A: Foundation Areas 
 These areas define how people, jobs, and organizations are represented in SuccessFactors Employee Central. 
 1. Job Architecture 
 Job codes, job families, levels and grades, job profiles, titles 

 Lift and shift 
 Carry the acquired company's job codes and titles into SuccessFactors as-is, utilizing existing job families and adding new. 

 Harmonize 
 Map all acquired roles into the parent's existing job architecture before load. 

 Focus areas 
 • Mapping Workday job profiles to EC job classifications 
 • Preserving FLSA/exempt status and EEO and other compliance fields 
 • Level calibration, pay range impact, and title changes if harmonizing 
 • Impact on compa-ratio for compensation module 

 Best practice 
 Lift and shift for Day 1 so harmonization can happen later without rework, unless the role mapping is obvious and already approved. 

 2. Organization Structure and Legal Entities 
 Supervisory orgs vs. departments, cost centers, legal entities, positions 

 Lift and shift 
 Recreate the acquired structure as a standalone branch in the parent's org tree. 

 Harmonize 
 Fold teams into the parent's departments, cost centers, and reporting lines. 

 Focus areas 
 • Legal entity and cost center setup (finance and payroll dependencies) 
 • Position management vs. non-position models 
 • Manager hierarchy accuracy and approval chains (OrgLab can be used to define future state reporting structure) 
 • Employees with dotted-line or matrix relationships 

 Best practice 
 Keep a clear structure as much as possible at go-live, then you can align in planned waves based upon finance and legal entity decisions. 

 3. Compensation and Benefits Structures 
 Pay grades, salary ranges, bonus plans, benefit plans, merit cycles 

 Lift and shift 
 Preserve existing pay structures and plan eligibility to honor commitments. 

 Harmonize 
 Move employees to the parent's structures and programs. 

 Focus areas 
 • There may be Legal or contractual obligations to maintain pay and benefits for a defined period 
 • Country-specific compensation plans 
 • Integration with payroll and benefits vendors 
 • Alignment of merit and bonus cycles with the go-live 

 Best practice 
 Cover the existing terms at transition. Harmonization can be done later with job architecture harmonization 

 4. Business Rules and Workflows 
 Approvals, hire/term/transfer rules,event reasons 

 Lift and shift 
 Replicate acquired company processes in SuccessFactors as closely as possible. 

 Harmonize 
 Adopt the parent's standard workflows and rules. 

 Focus areas 
 • Workday business processes do not map one-to-one to SF workflows and business rules 
 • Defaults such as work schedule hours at hire 
 • Termination logic and workflow conditions 
 • Event and reason code alignment 

 Best practice 
 Default to the parent's standard processes. Replicating acquired company logic in SF usually adds complexity at go-live. Make exceptions only for legal or country needs for a successful go-live 

 5. Security and Access (RBP) 
 Role-based permissions, groups, sensitive data, single sign-on 

 Lift and shift 
 Replicate the acquired company's security roles. 

 Harmonize 
 Build access on the parent's role and group model. 

 Focus areas 
 • Rebuild in RBP groups and roles rather than copying Workday/third party security to avoid continuing security policies that were not effective 
 • Target population groups for the acquired company 
 • Country-based restrictions 
 • Tighter controls sensitive data such as dependents, national IDs 

 Best practice 
 Always harmonize. Replicating another platform's security model is not recommended 

 6. Country Configuration and Compliance 
 New countries, statutory fields, data privacy, regulatory reporting 

 Lift and shift 
 Configure acquired countries as stand-alone setups with their own picklists, fields, and templates. 

 Harmonize 
 Align to the parent's country configurations where they already exist. 

 Focus areas 
 • Statutory fields and local labor law requirements 
 • New country setup where the parent has no footprint 
 • Document and contract templates by country 
 • Regulatory reporting continuity (for example EEO and VETS-4212 in the US) 
 • Data privacy requirements such as GDPR 

 Best practice 
 Build a country-by-country readiness checklist with local HR and Legal sign-off. Reuse the parent's configuration where it exists and add only the gaps. 

 7. Historical Data 
 Effective-dated history, archives, retention, right of access 

 Lift and shift 
 Load as much history as the data model allows. 

 Harmonize 
 Load current state record into SuccessFactors 

 Focus areas 
 • Full history should not be converted 
 • Retention policy and who can access the archive after transition 
 • GDPR right of access 
 • Former employees' future needs: tax, immigration, benefits, legal matters 

 Best practice 
 This is often underestimated and surfaces late, usually when a former employee or auditor asks for records that no longer exist in the new system. Define the retention and access model early: where history lives, who can access it, and how former employees can request their records. 

 Part B: Talent Modules 
 8. Performance and Goals Management (PMGM) 
 Goals, review cycles, ratings, calibration, feedback, development plans 
 Performance touches pay, promotion, and how employees feel about being evaluated by a new company. It is also closely scrutinized by works councils. 

 Lift and shift 
 Build separate templates, rating scales, and cycle dates in SF for the acquired population. 

 Harmonize 
 Assign acquired employees to the parent's existing forms, scale, and calendar. 

 Focus areas 
 • Template and permission assignment by population 
 • Rating scale crosswalk (for example 5-point to 4-point or 5-point to 5-point) – determine how past ratings map 
 • Route maps and calibration sessions that include the new group 
 • RBP visibility for ratings and feedback 
 • Performance history of employees 
 • Complete in flight cycle in legacy system 

 Best Practice 
 Honor the in-flight cycle through completion, then onboard the acquired population into the parent's process at the start of the next cycle. Build a rating scale crosswalk and archive historical ratings with controlled access. In Scenario B, skip building a temporary SF process if the parent will not use that module. 
 9. Recruitment and Talent Acquisition 
 Requisitions, candidates, offers, onboarding handoff, compliance reporting 
 Hiring does not pause on go-live day. Open requisitions, in-flight candidates, and offers must continue, and offers are legally sensitive. 

 Lift and shift 
 Create separate requisition templates, approval flows, and offer letter templates for the acquired population. 

 Harmonize 
 Use the parent's templates, workflows, and career site. 

 Focus areas 
 • Requisition and offer approval workflows 
 • Requisition templates tied to job architecture 
 • Onboarding handoff to EC and country-specific fields 

 Best Practice 
 Harmonize while protecting in-flight offers. 

 10. Learning 
 Catalog, curricula, assignments, transcripts, compliance training 

 Lift and shift 
 Migrate the acquired company's courses, curricula, and assignments. 

 Harmonize 
 Move the acquired population into the parent's catalog and assignment model. 

 Focus areas 
 • Completion records and certifications that are compliance-critical 
 • Assignment profiles and exclusion rules, so parent-company mandatory assignments do not flood the acquired population unintentionally 
 • Content licensing 
 • Access for employees and managers 

 Best practice 
 Migrate completion records for compliance-critical items only. Use exclusion rules to control assignments, then phase the acquired population into the parent catalog on a planned schedule. 

 Part C: Operations and Experience 
 These areas keep people paid, informed, and productive from the first day on the new platform. 
 11. Time Off and Work Schedules 
 Leave policies, accruals, balances, holiday calendars, default hours 

 Lift and shift 
 Recreate the acquired policies and accrual rules, and carry over balances. 

 Harmonize 
 Move to the parent's policies. 

 Focus areas 
 • Policy gaps in countries where the parent has no equivalent (manual tracking or a vendor solution) 
 • Work schedule defaults, such as hours defaulting at new hire 
 • Configure work schedules for time off calculations 
 • Holiday calendars by location 

 Best practice 
 Lift and shift at go-live. Changing leave policies mid-transition can create issues. Flag country gaps early and decide on manual or vendor tracking. 

 12. Employee Experience and Language Support 
 Self-service, mobile, documents, language, help desk, communications 

 Lift and shift 
 Provide a separate portal or landing experience for the acquired population. 

 Harmonize 
 Move employees to the parent's portal, mobile app, and support model. 

 Focus areas 
 • Employee and manager self-service readiness 
 • Language support gaps in the UI and translated job aids 
 • Help desk and case routing for the new population 
 • Communications and training before and after cutover 

 Best practice 
 Use the parent's company experience, and close language gaps before go-live. Translated materials also support the works council conversation.

items.title: Purchase Order Accruals calculation
items.author: Naveenk_S42024
items.text:
Dear All, 
 We onboard a consultant on a six-month contract with a daily rate of GBP 100. As per the contract agreement, the maximum billable days are limited to 22 days per month. 
 We do not use the Service Entry Sheet (SES) concept in SAP. Therefore, we need to manage the Purchase Order (PO) and monthly accrual postings without service entry confirmations. 
 We are facing the following challenges: 
 Scenario 1: Maintaining the PO quantity as 6 months 
 If we maintain the PO order quantity as six months, the system calculates the PO value based on 180 days × GBP 100, resulting in GBP 18,000. This is incorrect because the contractual maximum is 22 billable days per month. 
 The system also calculates accruals based on the actual calendar days in each month (30 or 31 days), resulting in incorrect accrual amounts. 
 Scenario 2: Maintaining the PO quantity as 132 days 
 If we maintain the PO order quantity as 132 days (22 days × 6 months), the PO value is correctly calculated as GBP 13,200. 
 However, the accrual calculation is still incorrect. For example, for October 2026, SAP calculates an accrual of GBP 3,100 (31 calendar days × GBP 100) instead of the expected GBP 2,200 (22 billable days × GBP 100). 
 Clarification Required 
 How can we achieve the correct PO valuation and monthly accrual calculations using standard SAP functionality, considering that we do not use Service Entry Sheets? 
 Our requirements are: 
 Maintain the PO value at GBP 13,200 for the six-month contract. 
 Calculate monthly accruals based on 22 billable days, resulting in GBP 2,200 per month. 
 Prevent the system from calculating accruals based on calendar days. 
 Use standard SAP PO and accrual functionality without custom development, wherever possible. 
 Please advise on the recommended standard SAP configuration and process to ensure that both the PO value and monthly accrual postings are aligned with the contractual terms, without using the Service Entry Sheet process. 

 Thanks 
 Naveen

From vision to reality: In 2026, SAP executives at SAP TechEd demonstrate how developers, customers, and partners can use SAP’s comprehensive AI tools and SAP Business AI Platform to build the Autonomous Enterprise. 
 SAP TechEd in 2026: The Autonomous Enterprise Becomes a Reality 

 Read the innovation news guide 

 In 1996 SAP held its first event for developers. Thirty years later in Berlin, SAP CTO Philipp Herzig told the SAP TechEd keynote audience, “We are experiencing the biggest and fastest technological shift in our lifetime.” 

 “For decades developers have been building systems in a structured, deterministic way. But the world for builders has changed tremendously with AI,” he said. “It changes what’s possible. This is what SAP TechEd is all about: combining both classical and new technologies that unlock the magic for business and provide endless opportunities to innovate.” 

 From vision to execution 

 Underscoring his point, Herzig noted that during the SAP Sapphire conference earlier this year, the company “put out a bold vision to enable the Autonomous Enterprise, re-imagining every business process end-to-end with AI. And just like 30 years ago, the whole tech stack is shifting.” 

 For SAP, this is reflected in Joule Work and the new SAP Business AI Platform. Herzig described Joule Work as a “groundbreaking new way to experience software” that taps into SAP’s five autonomous domains and assistants that reason and act across SAP and non-SAP data, and SAP Business AI Platform as “the foundation where you build and extend agents, manage all your data, and govern AI experiences.” 

 What’s New in AI, Joule and the Autonomous Enterprise | SAP TechEd 2026 

 Click the button below to load the content from YouTube. 

 Always allow YouTube 

 Video by Alex Januschke, Natalie Hauck, Rana Hamzakadi 

 Designed for better business outcomes 

 Elaborating, he emphasized that SAP Business AI Platform “isn’t just another tech platform, it’s specifically designed to build better business outcomes, deliver faster time-to-value and better price performance.” In addition, it is enterprise-readiness from day one: secure, governed, and compliant, “all made possible through our unique context layer built on 50 years of domain and industry expertise.” 

 Together, Joule Work and SAP Business AI Platform underpin SAP’s commitment to build the Autonomous Enterprise. “And it’s here today,” Herzig told the audience. “We are excited to show you our latest updates at SAP TechEd.” 

 For the rest of the keynote, Herzig and his SAP colleagues—including SAP Chief AI Officer Jonathan von Rueden; Manoj Swaminathan, president and chief product officer for SAP Autonomous Suite; Tina Berlin, head of AI Foundation EU at SAP; Michelle Niedernhuber, lead product manager for SAP AI Agent Hub; and Soeren Ruder, chief product officer and global head of Customer Experience & Solutions—detailed these updates and demonstrated them on stage.

 Joule Work

It remembers preferences and context from past interactions and continuously adapts.  Manoj Swaminathan then took the stage to demonstrate the SAP Autonomous Suite. “For over five decades, SAP has built the systems that help you run your business in the best way possible.  “I’m excited to announce today 40 assistants and 300 agents between SAP and our partners for you to explore,” he added. “These give you a baseline for systems of intelligence and systems of action, built around three priorities, delivering: automation, intelligence and insights, and optimizations, with value that can be realized and measured, across reduction in cost, increased productivity, increased speed, improved quality, and more.” 

 The new assistants include a Financial Consolidation Assistant that can reduce the time to close the books by up to 68%, a Sourcing Assistant that can reduce total cost of ownership by 15%, and a Supplier Management Assistant that detects and responds to supplier risk 60% faster.

 “You might ask, ‘I’m already doing this with support from public models, why build on top of SAP’s Business AI Platform?’ Because a public model does not know your processes, your master data or your company. SAP Business AI Platform does,” Swaminathan shared. “Our AI agents are embedded in the deterministic workflows of our applications. They deliver the one true answer as they run on the same data, following the same rules, and leave the same audit trail as our applications and you decide the level of autonomy.” 

 But he pointed out that the SAP Autonomous Suite does not restrict itself to only back-office operations. “Our biggest customers are losing 11% of revenue to unplanned downtime experiences with on-site operations. Customers understand the problem but there hasn’t been a solution that responds to these challenges until now.” 

 Physical AI by SAP 

 To address this issue, Swaminathan announced physical AI by SAP, which extends the Autonomous Enterprise into the physical world, turning business decisions into physical action, and bringing verified outcomes back into SAP in a secure and governed way. 

 During an on-stage appearance, Ricky Watts, who runs the Industrial and Robotics Division of Intel, said the company is already running physical AI at its operational site in Chengdu, where SAP warehouse management is driving autonomous robots closing the loop, writing outcomes back into SAP as live transactions. 

 Jonathan von Rueden then took over the keynote stage to talk about the more than 300 standard Joule agents across the suite and how Joule Work and skills can adapt and customize standard agents to get the most from AI. If you want to go further still, he said, “Joule Studio is just one click away.”

 Joule Studio, SAP’s agent-building platform, lets anyone customize AI with a skill: a natural language description and a few lines of code defining what an agent should do, opening agent-building beyond developers. 

 If you want to go deeper, and need to know where to begin, the Process Consulting Agent identifies where and what to build before development begins. “Just say what you want to get it done,” said von Rueden. SAP Knowledge Graph finds the relevant APIs, MCP servers, and data products, and Joule Studio generates the specifications, structure, and integration logic. 

 The result: Moving from intent to a working agent takes roughly 2.5 hours instead of 13. Because agents don’t need to guess at requests, they use fewer tokens. “In our testing, that adds up to 50% lower cost per task,” von Rueden told the audience. 

 “With Joule Studio on SAP Business AI platform, we focus on four things: business outcomes, time to value, performance for price, and enterprise readiness with deep integration.”

 “You’d expect a certain level of out-of-the-box capabilities and we’ve delivered,” he said. Agent gateway is generally available today, connecting agents and endpoints across any landscape boundary.” 

 For more complex scenarios requiring rate limiting, routing, protocol translation, and advanced access control, SAP is announcing SAP Enterprise AI Gateway, built on SAP Integration Suite as a natural overlay to agent gateway. 

 Herzig then returned to the stage to underscore the importance of reliable data for business AI. “Any AI system is only as good as the data it reasons over,” he said, “data that lives in different physical systems, be it SAP or non-SAP, on clouds, on-premise, and the edge.”

 In addition, he announced that the full scope of the entire Databricks platform will now be available natively in SAP Business Data Cloud. This means that data from different systems can now be combined into a “golden” master record, providing customers with a unified, AI-ready data foundation. 

 SAP executives also introduced a new SAP Business Data Cloud Ontology Manager, available as beta. With it, customers can enrich SAP Knowledge Graph with their industry-specific concepts or build entire ontologies.

Runtime verification enforcement ensures that agents not verified in SAP AI Agent Hub cannot be invoked.

 All of it is SAP-managed with governance built in: ISO and SOC compliant, runtime enforced, with every agent testable and traceable via SAP AI Agent Hub. And the new SAP Enterprise AI Gateway delivers policy enforcement, enhanced observability, and runtime controls all in one place.

items.title: SAP ABAP Purchase Order Release Audit Report with Document Flow Navigation
items.author: reddysekharpathipati
items.text:
Introduction: 
 If you work with SAP, you know that Purchase Orders (POs), Purchase Requisitions (PRs), and Long-Term Agreements (LTAs) almost always require an approval process, known as a release strategy. 
 When audit season rolls around, the same questions always pop up: 
 Who approved this document? When exactly did they do it? What level of approval was it? And how does it tie back to the original PR, LTA, or Sales Order? 
 Here is the frustrating part: SAP updates the current status in tables like EKKO and EBAN, but it doesn't easily show the historical "who" and "when." Since there is no out-of-the-box standard report that tracks this entire chain (PO → PR → LTA → SO), auditors usually have to dig through documents manually, one by one. 
 To solve this, I’ll show you how to build a custom PO Release Audit Report in ABAP. This report captures the approver's user ID, full name, exact date, time, and approval level. Plus, it features a clean, single-screen ALV grid using CL_SALV_TABLE—allowing you to click and drill down into the details, and jump back with a single click, completely eliminating annoying pop-up windows. 

 Solution Review: 
 Solution at a Glance 
 The report reads the release status and its change history, finds the linked documents, and shows everything in one ALV where each click goes one level deeper. 
 Selection screen (PO / PR / LTA / SO)
 │
 ▼
 GET_DATA ──► starting documents (EKKO / EBAN / VBAK)
 │
 ▼
GET_RELEASE_HISTORY ──► CDHDR + CDPOS + USER_ADDR
 │
 ▼
 ALV display (CL_SALV_TABLE)
 │
 click Document No. click Source
 │ │
 ▼ ▼
 DO_DRILL DO_BACK
 (GET_CHAIN → next level) (restore previous list) 
 Design Decisions 
 Release data from change documents 
 EKKO and EBAN hold only the current release status (FRGZU). The user, date and time are in the change documents: 
 CDHDR has the username, date and time. 
 CDPOS has the new value of FRGZU. 
 USER_ADDR has the full name. 
 The report uses object class EINKBELEG for PO and LTA, and BANF for PR. 

 Same ALV, no popup 
 Instead of opening a new ALV each time, the report replaces the data and refreshes the same grid. Popups are avoided because they stack up and are harder to navigate. 

 Advantages 
 One report instead of checking ME23N, ME53N, VA03 and change documents one by one. 
 Shows release user, date, time and level together. 
 Follows the whole PO → PR → LTA → SO chain. 
 Simple navigation, with no popups. 
 The history-stack pattern is reusable in other ALV reports. 

 Step 1: Output structure 
 TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_out,
 lvl TYPE n LENGTH 1, " PO=1 PR=2 LTA=3 SO=4
 source TYPE char3,
 docno TYPE char10,
 doctype TYPE char4,
 erdat TYPE erdat,
 ernam TYPE ernam,
 frggr TYPE ekko-frggr,
 frgsx TYPE ekko-frgsx,
 frgke TYPE ekko-frgke,
 frgzu TYPE ekko-frgzu,
 rel_level TYPE char2,
 uname TYPE cdhdr-username,
 fullname TYPE user_addr-name_textc,
 udate TYPE cdhdr-udate,
 utime TYPE cdhdr-utime,
 objcl TYPE cdhdr-objectclas, " helper (hidden)
 objid TYPE cdhdr-objectid, " helper (hidden)
 END OF ty_out. 
 Step 2: Selection screen 
 Fields appear or disappear depending on the radio button: AT SELECTION-SCREEN OUTPUT.
 LOOP AT SCREEN.
 CASE screen-group1.
 WHEN 'PO'.
 IF r_po = 'X'. screen-active = 1. ELSE. screen-active = 0. ENDIF.
 WHEN 'PR'.
 IF r_pr = 'X'. screen-active = 1. ELSE. screen-active = 0. ENDIF.
 WHEN 'LTA'.
 IF r_lta = 'X'. screen-active = 1. ELSE. screen-active = 0. ENDIF.
 WHEN 'SO'.
 IF r_so = 'X'. screen-active = 1. ELSE. screen-active = 0. ENDIF.
 ENDCASE.
 MODIFY SCREEN.
 ENDLOOP. 
 Step 3: Read the starting documents. 
 WHEN r_po.
 SELECT ebeln, bsart, aedat, ernam, frggr, frgsx, frgke, frgzu
 FROM ekko
 WHERE ebeln IN @s_ebeln
 AND aedat IN @s_aedat
 AND bsart IN @s_bsart
 AND bstyp = 'F'
 INTO TABLE @DATA (lt_po). 
 PR, LTA and SO follow the same pattern, using EBAN, EKKO (bstyp K or L) and VBAK. 
 Step 4: Release history 
 SELECT objectclas, objectid, changenr, username, udate, utime
 FROM cdhdr
 FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT _keys
 WHERE objectclas = @LT _keys-objectclas
 AND objectid = @LT _keys-objectid
 INTO TABLE @DATA (lt_hdr).

SELECT objectclas, objectid, changenr, tabname, fname, value_new
 FROM cdpos
 FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @LT _hdr
 WHERE objectclas = @LT _hdr-objectclas
 AND objectid = @LT _hdr-objectid
 AND changenr = @LT _hdr-changenr
 AND tabname IN ('EKKO', 'EBAN')
 AND fname = 'FRGZU'
 INTO TABLE @DATA (lt_pos). 
 The release level is the number of X characters in the new status: lv_cnt = count( val = ls_pos-value_new sub = 'X' ).
IF lv_cnt > 0.
 ls_final-rel_level = |{ lv_cnt }|.
ENDIF. 
 Step 5: Find linked documents 
 From To Link
PO PR EKPO-BANFN
PO or PR LTA EKPO-KONNR, EBAN-KONNR
LTA or PO SO EKKN-VBELN
PR SO EBKN-VBELN, VBEP-BANFN" PO -> PR
SELECT DISTINCT banfn FROM ekpo

" keep only real agreements (contract K / scheduling agreement L)
SELECT ebeln FROM ekko

 Step 6: ALV with hotspots: 
 cl_salv_table=>factory( IMPORTING r_salv_table = go_alv
 CHANGING t_table = gt_out ).

" DOCNO = go down one level
lo_col_tab ?= lo_cols->get_column( 'DOCNO' ).
lo_col_tab->set_cell_type( if_salv_c_cell_type=>hotspot ).

" SOURCE = go back one level

lo_col_tab->set_cell_type( if_salv_c_cell_type=>hotspot ).

" hide helper columns
lo_cols->get_column( 'OBJCL' )->set_visible( abap_false ).

lo_cols->get_column( 'LVL' )->set_visible( abap_false ).

SET HANDLER go_handler->on_link_click FOR lo_events. 
 Step 7: Click handler 
 METHOD on_link_click.
 CASE column.
 WHEN 'DOCNO'. PERFORM do_drill USING row.

 ENDCASE.
ENDMETHOD. 
 Step 8: Drill down (one level per click) 

 CASE ls_row-source.
 WHEN 'PO'. lv_next = 'PR'.
 WHEN 'PR'. lv_next = 'LTA'.

ENDCASE.

PERFORM get_chain USING ls_row-source ls_row-docno

DELETE lt_new WHERE source <> lv_next. " keep ONLY the next level

" remember the current level
ls_hist-title = gv_title.
ls_hist-data = gt_out.
APPEND ls_hist TO gt_hist.

" show the next level in the SAME alv
gt_out = lt_new.
gv_title = lv_title.
PERFORM refresh_alv. 
 Step 9: Refresh the same ALV: 
 FORM refresh_alv.
 go_alv->get_display_settings( )->set_list_header( gv_title ).
 go_alv->get_columns( )->set_optimize( abap_true ).
 go_alv->refresh( ).
ENDFORM. 
 Step:10 Display *&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Form DISPLAY_ALV (single full-screen ALV, no popup)
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM display_alv.

 DATA: lo_cols TYPE REF TO cl_salv_columns_table,
 lo_col_tab TYPE REF TO cl_salv_column_table,
 lo_events TYPE REF TO cl_salv_events_table.

 IF gt_out IS INITIAL.
 MESSAGE 'No data found for the given selection' TYPE 'S' DISPLAY LIKE 'W'.
 RETURN.
 ENDIF.

 TRY.
 cl_salv_table=>factory( IMPORTING r_salv_table = go_alv
 CHANGING t_table = gt_out ).

 go_alv->get_display_settings( )->set_striped_pattern( abap_true ).

 PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'DOCTYPE' 'Doc.Type' 'Doc. Type' 'Document Type'.

 PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'ERNAM' 'Created By' 'Created By' 'Created By'.
 PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FRGGR' 'Rel.Group' 'Release Group' 'Release Group'.
 PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FRGSX' 'Rel.Strat.' 'Rel. Strategy' 'Release Strategy'.
 PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FRGKE' 'Rel.Ind.' 'Rel. Indicator' 'Release Indicator'.
 PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FRGZU' 'Rel.Status' 'Release Status' 'Release Status'.
 PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'REL_LEVEL' 'Rel.Level' 'Release Level' 'Release Level'.
 PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'UNAME' 'User ID' 'User ID' 'User ID'.
 PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'FULLNAME' 'Full Name' 'Full Name' 'Full Name'.
 PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'UDATE' 'Rel.Date' 'Release Date' 'Release Date'.
 PERFORM set_col USING lo_cols 'UTIME' 'Rel.Time' 'Release Time' 'Release Time'.

 " hide helper columns
 lo_cols->get_column( 'OBJCL' )->set_visible( abap_false ).
 lo_cols->get_column( 'OBJID' )->set_visible( abap_false ).
 lo_cols->get_column( 'LVL' )->set_visible( abap_false ).

 " SOURCE = hotspot: go BACK one level

items.title: Manage Flexible Constraints for SAP Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling (SAP PP/DS)
items.author: MaryiaT
items.text:
Manage Flexible Constraints for SAP PP/DS 
 Plan Transparently. Control Production Consumption. Adapt to Change. 
 Introduction 
 Effective production planning requires more than balancing supply and demand. Planners also need transparency, control over production and procurement quantities, and the flexibility to adapt plans to changing business requirements. 
 Previously planners did not have complete visibility of all the key information such as KPIs, alerts etc. across different phases of planning such as tactical planning (SAP Integrated Business Planning) and operational planning (Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling for SAP S/4HANA). ​Without a consistent way to communicate planning limits and targets, decisions made in one system may be overwritten or not fully respected in another. 
 Flexible Constraints in SAP PP/DS address this challenge by allowing planners to define supply-related targets and limits that are considered during production planning. 
 Introduced with SAP S/4HANA OP2023 FPS2, this functionality has been further enhanced and optimized in subsequent releases, including OP2025 FPS2. These enhancements provide additional capabilities for managing constraints, handling large volumes of data, and controlling how constraints influence planning decisions. 
 In this post, we will explore the main concepts behind Flexible Constraints, their configuration and management in the Fiori application, and the key enhancements introduced in SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1. 
 ​ 1. What Are Flexible Constraints? 
 Flexible Constraints are supply-related limits and targets considered during planning in SAP PP/DS. They help planners control how much supply should be planned for a specific product and location or for a particular source of supply. 
 Flexible Constraints support two main planning scenarios: 
 Integration with an external planning system: Flexible Constraints defined in an external planning system can be integrated into PP/DS using an OData service or a remote-enabled function module. 
 Local maintenance in SAP S/4HANA: Flexible Constraints can also be created and maintained directly in SAP S/4HANA PP/DS. 
 This approach helps ensure that prebuild and post-build decisions made by planners are reflected in operational planning and remain consistent across planning systems. 
 2. Main Types and Principles 
 Flexible Constraints define the desired or permitted supply quantities for a given planning period. Three types of quantity semantics are available: 
 Target Supply (soft constraint): Defines the desired supply quantity. 
 Minimum Supply (hard constraint): Defines the minimum supply quantity to be considered during planning. 
 Maximum Supply (hard constraint): Defines the maximum supply quantity to be considered during planning. 
 These values help planners communicate their supply expectations while distinguishing between preferred quantities and mandatory planning limits. 
 2.1. Recurrence and Time Buckets 
 Flexible Constraints can be maintained for different recurring time intervals: 
 Daily 
 Weekly 
 Monthly 
 Quarterly 
 Yearly 
 Custom, for example, biweekly 
 The selected recurrence determines the time buckets for which the constraints apply. 
 2.2. Granularity Levels 
 Granularity determines how specifically a Flexible Constraint applies. SAP PP/DS supports two main levels: 
 LOCPRD — Location Product 
 The constraint applies to a product at a specific location, independently of the individual source of supply. 
 LOCPRDSOS — Location Product Source of Supply 
 The constraint applies to a specific product, location, and source of supply. 
 LOCPRDSOS can be further divided into internal and external sources of supply. 
 LOCPRDSOS Internal 
 An internal source of supply represents in-house production based on the Production Data Structure (PDS). The relevant production source is determined using the material's MRP 3 settings, including the production version. 
 LOCPRDSOS External 
 An external source of supply represents external procurement and is based on the material's procurement settings and the relevant source of supply. 
 The supported external source-of-supply categories include: 
 Info Record 
 Scheduling Agreement 
 Subcontracting 
 Stock Transfer 
 The choice between LOCPRD and LOCPRDSOS depends on the level of control required. LOCPRD provides an overall supply target or limit for a product at a location, whereas LOCPRDSOS enables more detailed control over individual supply sources. 
 2.3. Planning Versions 
 Flexible Constraints can be used with either the active planning version (000) or an inactive planning version. 
 Using the active planning version supports operational planning, while an inactive planning version allows planners to simulate alternative scenarios and evaluate their impact without directly changing the active plan. 
 3. How Are Flexible Constraints Used in Planning? 
 Flexible Constraints are consumed during production planning through the SAP_PP_FLXC heuristic , which is built on top of the Standard Lots Heuristic. 
 The heuristic considers the relevant Flexible Constraints during its planning run, helping align planned supply with the defined minimum, target, and maximum quantities. 
 From SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1 onward, priority and penalty settings provide additional ways to influence how Flexible Constraints are considered during planning. 
 4. Manage Flexible Constraints for PP/DS — Fiori App F7726 
 The SAP Fiori application F7726 — Manage Flexible Constraints for PP/DS provides a central interface for creating, updating, copying, deleting, and processing Flexible Constraints. 
 Let's look at the main functions available in the application. 
 4.1. Creation 
 Flexible Constraints Group IDs are created from the list page of the Manage Flexible Constraints for PP/DS application by selecting Create . 

 All mandatory fields must be completed before the constraint group can be created 

 The application validates overlapping periods. Flexible Constraints cannot be created for the same location-product scope for an overlapping time period. If an overlap is detected, a validation error is displayed, and the new FLXC Group ID is not created. 
 4.2. Update 
 Existing Flexible Constraints can be edited, provided the following value relationship is maintained: 

 Minimum FLXC ≤ Target FLXC ≤ Maximum FLXC 
 Two different meanings can be represented by a value of zero: 
 Zero with a unit of measure (UoM): The constraint is explicitly maintained with a value of zero. 
 Zero without a UoM: The constraint value is not maintained. 
 This distinction is important when interpreting and updating constraint data. 
 The active or inactive status is maintained at the individual bucket level. Active buckets participate in planning, while inactive buckets are excluded. If necessary, a bucket can be deactivated in Edit mode. 
 4.3. Copy 
 The application provides three options for copying Flexible Constraints from the list page. These options allow planners to reuse existing planning logic while adapting the constraints to different products or locations. 
 Copy from Template 
 The constraint is copied on a one-to-one basis to another target product location. During copying, the planning version, priority, and period can be changed. 

 Absolute values 
 Minimum, Target, and Maximum values can be entered directly for the target product location. 

 Relative to Template 
 Minimum, Target, and Maximum values for the target product location can be maintained as percentages of the corresponding values from the source product location. 

 4.4. Deletion 
 Deletion functionality for Flexible Constraints was introduced with SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1. 
 The application provides several deletion options, depending on the object and the data to be removed. 
 Delete from the List Page 
 Past and inactive FLXC Group IDs can be deleted from the list page using the Delete button. 
 Delete from the Object Page 
 An inactive FLXC Group ID can be deleted from its object page using the Delete button. 
 Delete All Inactive and Past Constraints 
 Within an FLXC Group ID, inactive or past buckets can be removed using the dedicated Delete All Inactive and Past Constraints button on the object page. 
 These options help maintain clean and manageable Flexible Constraints data. 
 5. Managing Large Volumes of Flexible Constraints 
 When Flexible Constraints need to be maintained for many products, locations, or sources of supply, manual processing can become inefficient. 
 The Manage Flexible Constraints for PP/DS application provides Excel-based functions to simplify mass creation, download, and update activities. 
 5.1. Get Template 
 Select Get Template on the list page to download the Excel template. 
 The workbook includes an additional page with instructions for preparing Flexible Constraints data. 
 5.2. Create from Excel 
 After entering the required data into the Excel template, upload the file using Create from Excel . 
 Both LOCPRD and LOCPRDSOS records can be created through this function. For large volumes of data, processing takes place in the background, resulting in the creation of new FLXC Group IDs. 
 If the uploaded file contains incorrect data or overlaps with existing records, the system displays validation errors to indicate where corrections are required. 
 5.3. Download in Excel 
 To export existing Flexible Constraints, select the required Group IDs on the list page and choose Download in Excel . The resulting workbook is downloaded to the local computer. 
 Starting with SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1, the download functionality provides two enhanced Excel files containing the main Flexible Constraints parameters, together with an additional Excel file containing priority and penalty attributes. 
 5.4. Update from Excel 
 Existing Flexible Constraints data can be updated in the downloaded Excel files, subject to the applicable Flexible Constraints logic and validations. 
 After making the required changes, upload the relevant file using Update from Excel . 
 These Excel-based capabilities make it easier to manage large datasets while retaining system validation of the uploaded information. 
 6. Priority — An Enhancement Introduced in OP2025 FPS1 
 Starting with SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1, each Flexible Constraints Group ID includes a Priority section. 
 Priorities range from A to O: 
 A: Highest priority 
 O: Lowest priority 
 A newly created FLXC Group ID is assigned priority A by default. 
 Priority can be maintained when creating an FLXC Group ID or updated later using the Edit function. 

 How Does Priority Influence Planning? 
 Priority settings are used by the SAP_PP_FLXC heuristic during planning. 
 By default, the heuristic considers the highest priority, A. However, planners can select another priority from the available list. 
 During a heuristic run, the selected priority and all higher priorities are considered by the Flexible Constraints planning logic. Constraints outside the considered priority range are ignored by the heuristic. 
 This functionality provides additional control over which Flexible Constraints influence a particular planning run. 

 7. Penalty — An Enhancement Introduced in OP2025 FPS1 
 Another enhancement introduced with SAP S/4HANA OP2025 FPS1 is the Penalty section. 
 Penalty settings can be maintained when creating or updating Flexible Constraints. This section is optional and can be left blank. 
 The object page of an FLXC Group ID provides the following penalty types and indicators. 
 7.1. Available Penalty Types 
 Below Minimum Supply 
 Penalty value: Free-value input field 
 Minimum Supply Penalty Indicator: Active or Inactive 
 Deviating Target Supply 
 Penalty value: Free-value input field 
 Target Supply Penalty Indicator: 
 Active Below and Exceeding Target Supply 
 Active Below Target Supply 
 Active Exceeding Target Supply 
 Inactive 
 Above Maximum Supply 
 Penalty value: Free-value input field 
 Max

items.title: Data Challenges in M&A HRIS Migrations: Lessons from a Workday to SuccessFactors Integration
items.author: manubhutani
items.text:
Data Challenges in M&A HRIS Migrations: Lessons from a Workday to SuccessFactors Integration 
 Purpose and context 
 Data is the most common source of schedule risk in an M&A HRIS migration. This document captures the categories of data challenges we have faced or should expect in such an engagement, where the acquired workforce moves from Workday into the parent company SAP SuccessFactors system, targeting a fixed go-live date. 
 Acquired data arrives built for another company's processes, naming conventions and legal context. The challenges below apply to most M&A integrations, with examples. 
 Challenges at a glance 
 Seven categories drive most of the rework: model mismatch, data quality, country variation, privacy and legal limits, integrations, historical data, and process ownership. 

 Category 
 Typical issue 
 Impact 
 Mitigation 

 Data model mismatch 
 Workday objects may not have one-to-one match in SF EC (org, position, business partner, roles) 
 Rework of mappings and load templates 
 Early mapping workshops, documented transformation rules 

 Data quality 
 Duplicates, missing mandatory fields, inconsistent formats 
 Failed loads, repeated cycles 
 Profiling and cleansing before first load, owner sign-off 

 Global variation 
 In a global environment, countries with different time off, local fields and statutory data 
 Gaps in policy, manual tracking 
 Country by country inventory, phased scope decisions 

 Privacy and Works Council 
 Restrictions on what data moves, who sees it and how long it is kept 
 Delays, scope changes 
 Early engagement, translated job aids, agreed access rules 

 Integrations 
 Other systems like Recruitment vendors (e.g., iCIMS), SSO, provisioning and vendors depend on final IDs and codes 
 Vendor delays and availability 
 Interface inventory, early credentialing and test data 

 Historical data 
 Not all history is migrated or accessible after cutover 
 Audit and employee-relations risk 
 Retention decision, archive or read-only access 

 Process and ownership 
 Unclear data owners, compressed load cycles, offline workarounds 
 Late surprises, weak audit trail 
 Named owners, load calendar, reconciliation checkpoints 

 Source and target data model differences 
 Workday and SF EC organize the same business facts differently, so conversion is a redesign of the data, not a copy. 
 Org structure: Workday supervisory orgs, cost centers and company hierarchies must be reshaped into EC legal entities, business units, divisions and departments. Departments need codes that follow the acquirer's conventions, and the acquired set must not collide with existing ones. 
 Code generation: Auto-sequenced department codes can repeat values that already exist. Because the next value on the sequence object is not editable, the workaround is to import a sequence record carrying the latest existing code so the next generated code is unique. 
 Position and person relationships: Position-to-person lookups, position-based reporting lines and vacant positions behave differently, and Workday managers may not map cleanly to EC positions. 
 Business Partner model: HR and other business partner relationships need to be rebuilt in EC, including who each relationship applies to. 
 Workflow roles: Workday approval chains become EC workflows driven by Dynamic Roles. Approver data must be complete and current or routing fails. 
 Time objects: Time Profile, Work Schedule and Holiday Calendar interact, and a wrong assignment on one affects the others. 
 Picklists and reference data: Job codes, job families, pay grades, locations and reason codes need crosswalks from the acquired company's values to the acquirer's values. 
 Mapping challenges and best practices 
 Most of these are decisions rather than technical tasks, and several need data from more than one source system (HCM, time tracking, payroll, benefits). Gathering it takes time, so start these discussions early. 
 1. Organization structures differ 
 Challenge: The acquired and parent systems define organizations differently, with different levels, names, codes and ownership of cost centers. 
 Best practice: Start from the parent company's org model and fit the acquired units into it, not the reverse. Decide early whether each unit maps to an existing org object or needs a new one, keep the legacy org as a crosswalk, agree naming and code conventions, and design the future-state reporting hierarchy with HR and finance sign-off. 
 2. Job architecture: harmonize or lift and shift 
 Challenge: The choice drives job codes, job families, pay grades and pay ranges. Lift and shift loads the acquired structures as they are, which is faster and changes little for employees, but it creates a parallel structure to clean up later. Harmonizing maps everyone to the parent's architecture, which is cleaner but needs compensation, legal and employee-relations review because titles and grades can affect pay, benefits and consultation requirements. 
 Best practice: Decide the approach before mapping starts and document it. A common pattern is lift and shift for day one with a planned harmonization later. If harmonizing, map with the job profile owners, validate grades and ranges, and confirm the impact on downstream payroll. 
 3. Work schedules and time off policies 
 Challenge: Policies and schedules differ by country. The parent may run Time Off in SuccessFactors for some countries and not others. Work schedules can also drive shift differentials in downstream payroll, so the parent may need schedule patterns that do not exist in the acquired HCM system. 
 Best practice: Build a country-by-country inventory early. For each country, confirm where schedules, accruals and balances are held, whether the country will use SuccessFactors Time Off, and which schedule patterns payroll needs. Request data from time, payroll and HCM owners early, because it comes from different systems. 
 4. Location mapping 
 Challenge: When the parent acquires a division and not every location in it, only some locations come over. Facilities must map the transferring employees to the parent's locations, and this can take time because approvals are often required. 
 Best practice: Agree the in-scope employee and location list early. Decide whether each location maps to an existing parent location or becomes a new one, and get facility owner approvals in parallel. Remember that location often drives time zone, holiday calendar and legal entity. 
 5. Number ranges and legacy employee IDs 
 Challenge: If the acquired company keeps running some downstream systems under a Transition Services Agreement (TSA), those systems still use the legacy employee ID. 
 Best practice: Agree number ranges up front to avoid collisions. Store the legacy ID against the new employee ID, make the crosswalk available to integrations, and set an end date and an owner for retiring it when the TSA ends. 
 6. Business email 
 Challenge: The acquired company's business email is usually not carried over, because new emails are created. Downstream systems may still need the parent company email. 
 Best practice: Decide the source of truth and timing for the new email, load it into the parent system, and keep it available for integrations such as SSO and provisioning. Keep the legacy email only where TSA systems need it. 
 7. Pay components 
 Challenge: Pay components rarely map one to one. The acquired company may split base pay, allowances, bonuses and differentials differently, with different frequencies, currencies, taxability and payroll treatment. Some components have no equivalent in the parent, and payroll expects specific codes. 
 Best practice: Build a pay component crosswalk with compensation and payroll owners. Decide for each component whether to map it, create a new one, or keep it in payroll only. Validate with sample employees and annual totals before the first load. 
 8. Dependents 
 Challenge: Dependents may be needed for benefits enrollment, tax or social insurance calculations, and leave or benefit rules in some countries. They may not be needed when benefits run through a separate vendor or when privacy and works council rules limit collection. The acquired HCM system often does not store them, so getting the data can take a long time. 
 Best practice: Decide by country whether dependents are required for go-live, and identify where the data lives today. If not required, collect it after go-live through employee self-service. Have legal and privacy review any collection. 
 9. Required fields differ between systems 
 Challenge: The acquired company's data model and processes differ, so fields required in the parent system may be optional in the source and left blank. 
 Best practice: Run a required-field gap analysis early. For each gap, decide whether to collect the data, derive it, or use a default, and name an owner. Avoid placeholder values that pollute reports later. 
 Data quality and completeness 
 Acquired data is usually good enough to run a company but not good enough to load without cleansing. 
 Missing mandatory fields: EC requires values (job, location, FTE, pay and work schedule data) that the source system may have left blank or stored in free text. 
 Duplicates and conflicts: The same person, department or position can exist twice, or collide with existing acquirer records and IDs. 
 Inconsistent formats: Dates, phone numbers, addresses, names and special characters differ by country and often fail validation on load. 
 Stale or inaccurate records: Terminated, inactive or future-dated records, outdated manager assignments and orphaned positions inflate load errors. 
 Compensation and job data: Pay components, currencies, frequencies and grade structures do not align with the acquirer's structures and need a mapping decision, not just a transformation. 
 Unclear ownership: When no one owns a data element, cleansing questions go unanswered and the same defects reappear in each load cycle. 
 The practical effect is repeated load-and-fix cycles. Profiling the source before the first load, and agreeing on what is fixed in Workday versus transformed in the load file, shortens those cycles. 
 Global and country-specific challenges 
 The acquired workforce spans many countries, so a single global design rarely fits every local requirement. 
 Time Off policies: The acquired company's policies across dozens of countries did not map to the acquirer's Time Off setup. This left a gap that forced a choice between manual tracking and a vendor solution. 
 Local and statutory data: Country-specific fields, national IDs, work permits, and works agreement terms need a home in EC or a documented exception. 
 Works Council (Germany): Engagement is recurring and covers data privacy, what historical data managers can see, comparisons of manager actions in Workday and SF, and the translation of job aids and the Works Agreement into German. 
 Data privacy: Cross-border transfer, access by role and retention limits constrain what is loaded and who can view it, and they can change scope late. 
 Offline workarounds: Proposals such as offline performance calibration raise legal, privacy and audit-trail risk and should be reviewed before being adopted. 
 Integration, security and downstream dependencies 
 Every downstream system depends on EC data being final and correct, so data defects surface as integration defects. 
 SSO and provisioning: Acquired employees need identities, SSO and account provisioning aligned to EC person and employment records, which depends on clean email, ID and status data. 
 Role-Based Permissions (RBP): Permission groups rely on org, location and job attributes. Poor source data produces wrong access, either too broad or too narrow. 
 Payroll, benefits and other vendors: Each interface has its own format and validation rules, and each needs test data that reflects real acquired-company scenarios. 
 Test scripts: Scripts need realistic, correct dat
