items.title: RAP unmanaged BO: BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CONFIRM_DEC dumps in saver – best approach?
items.author: SiHyeon_Park28
items.text:
Hello, 
 I'm building a Fiori Elements app (OData V4, RAP) that posts goods issue (PGI) for outbound deliveries, and I'd like advice on which approach is most appropriate. 
 Environment 
 SAP S/4HANA 2023 FPS03 on-premise (S4CORE 108 SP03), SAP_BASIS 7.58 SP03 
 Standard ABAP package (not ABAP Cloud) 
 Why I can't use a released RAP BO 
 I_OutboundDeliveryTP / R_OutboundDeliveryTP only offer CreateDlvFromSalesDocument and CreateDlvItemFromSalesDocument . There is no PGI action, header update is not enabled, and OverallGoodsMovementStatus / ActualGoodsMovementDate are read-only. 
 I_MaterialDocumentTP can create a material document, but it doesn't update the delivery status, document flow, or billing due index, so it doesn't replace delivery-based PGI. 
 So I use BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CONFIRM_DEC with HEADER_CONTROL-POST_GI_FLG = 'X' in an unmanaged BO (read-only list of deliveries + one instance action postGoodsIssue , no own persistence, no draft). 
 Problem 
 My first version called the BAPI in the saver's save method. It works when PGI succeeds. When the BAPI hits a business error, it ends with BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT : 
 LSC_ZI_PGI_CR=>SAVE
 -> BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CONFIRM_DEC (SAPLV50I)
 -> FORM ROLLBACK_CHECK (LV50IF01)
 >>>>> ROLLBACK WORK. 
 The BAPI executes ROLLBACK WORK itself on error, which is forbidden in the RAP save phase. The user only sees "ABAP Runtime error 'BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT'" and never the real error message. 
 Options I'm considering 
 A) sRFC in the action handler (current solution) 
 In the action handler (interaction phase) I call the BAPI with DESTINATION 'NONE' , then BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT / BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK in the same RFC session, and then RFC_CONNECTION_CLOSE . The saver does nothing. 
 CALL FUNCTION 'BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CONFIRM_DEC'
 DESTINATION 'NONE'
 EXPORTING header_data = ls_header header_control = ls_control delivery = iv_vbeln
 TABLES return = lt_return
 EXCEPTIONS system_failure = 1 MESSAGE lv_msg communication_failure = 2 MESSAGE lv_msg OTHERS = 3.
" no error -> BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT DESTINATION 'NONE', else BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK DESTINATION 'NONE' 
 Pros: no dump. Standard messages (e.g. M7 021 stock deficit, delivery locked, missing CO account assignment) are returned to the UI immediately. 
 Cons: PGI is committed outside the RAP LUW, so a later ROLLBACK ENTITIES or a failure elsewhere in the same request cannot undo it. I also can't lock the delivery in the RAP lock method, because the RFC session is a different lock owner and the BAPI would collide with it. 
 B) BAPI in the saver, accept dumps on error 
 Keep the BAPI in save so PGI is part of the RAP LUW and RAP commits it. To reduce dumps I added pre-checks in the action handler: lock ( ENQUEUE_EVVBLKE ), picking/GI status, storage location, MM period (MARV), and unrestricted stock (MARD/MCHB). 
 Pros: transactionally consistent with RAP. 
 Cons: any error the pre-checks don't anticipate still dumps. In my test, a delivery passed all pre-checks but failed because of a missing CO account assignment (OKB9), and it dumped. The BAPI has no test/simulation mode I could call in check_before_save . 
 C) bgPF 
 Register the PGI in save with cl_bgmc_process_factory and run it after the RAP commit using an uncontrolled operation ( IF_BGMC_OP_SINGLE_TX_UNCONTR ), since the BAPI needs to roll back on its own. 
 Pros: runs only if the RAP transaction commits. 
 Cons: asynchronous, so the user doesn't get the result or error immediately, and I'd need extra logging/status handling. I also found a hint that RAP should use controlled operations ( set_operation ), but a controlled operation would dump on the BAPI's ROLLBACK WORK again. 
 Questions 
 For a legacy BAPI that executes ROLLBACK WORK internally, which approach is recommended or supported in RAP: A, B, C, or something else? 
 Is a synchronous RFC ( DESTINATION 'NONE' ) in the interaction phase of an unmanaged BO considered acceptable, or is it expected to be restricted by runtime checks in later releases? 
 Is registering an uncontrolled bgPF operation from the RAP save phase allowed? 
 Is there a released API or a newer RAP BO for outbound delivery PGI that I missed? 
 Thank you in advance!

items.author: ayearis

Hi SAP Community, 
 I’m exploring an application that would use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to interact with SAP HANA, and I’d like to understand SAP’s guidance on this approach. 
 The architecture I have in mind is: 
 AI application / MCP client → custom MCP server → SAP HANA 
 The MCP server would expose tools that let the application request data from HANA. Before moving forward, I want to understand whether direct database access is appropriate, what restrictions apply, and whether a different integration approach would be preferable. 
 My main questions are: 

 SAP’s approach to MCP: Are there official SAP MCP servers, supported integrations, or reference architectures for this scenario? 

 Direct database access: What restrictions or support considerations apply when a custom MCP server queries HANA directly? How does this differ between a standalone HANA database and HANA underlying an SAP application such as SAP S/4HANA? 

 Recommended integration path: When should I use database access versus released APIs, OData services, or an application layer on SAP BTP? 

 Security and authorizations: How should user permissions be enforced across the MCP layer? Could direct SQL access bypass business-level authorization checks, even when database permissions are configured correctly? 

 Operational and contractual concerns: Could this approach introduce issues involving SAP support, licensing, upgrades, performance, or data governance? Would restricting the integration to read-only operations materially change these considerations? 
 I’m also interested in whether the recommended approach is to expose narrowly scoped tools with predefined queries rather than allow AI-generated SQL. 
 My goal is to understand the boundaries before committing to an implementation and avoid an architecture that works technically but creates problems later.

69.summary: A developer building a Fiori Elements (OData V4) app on RAP in an unmanaged BO needs to post goods issue for outbound deliveries on S/4HANA 2023 FPS03 with standard ABAP (not ABAP Cloud). The standard BAPI BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CONFIRM_DEC runs ROLLBACK WORK internally on business errors, which causes BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT when called from the saver. The author compares three options: a synchronous RFC with its own commit/rollback in the interaction phase, pre-checks with the BAPI kept in save, and a background process via bgPF. The author asks four questions about support, RFC use, uncontrolled bgPF, and released APIs.
key_points: Environment: S/4HANA 2023 FPS03 on-premise (S4CORE 108 SP03, SAP_BASIS 7.58 SP03), standard ABAP package, not ABAP Cloud
Released RAP BOs (I_OutboundDeliveryTP, R_OutboundDeliveryTP) offer no PGI action, and I_MaterialDocumentTP does not update delivery status or document flow
BAPI call in the saver dumps with BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT because ROLLBACK_CHECK (LV50IF01) executes ROLLBACK WORK
Option A: sRFC with DESTINATION 'NONE' in the action handler, then BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT/ROLLBACK, gives clean messages but commits outside the RAP LUW
Option B: keep the BAPI in save with pre-checks (ENQUEUE_EVVBLKE, MARV, MARD/MCHB), but unanticipated errors such as a missing OKB9 CO account assignment still dump
Option C: cl_bgmc_process_factory with IF_BGMC_OP_SINGLE_TX_UNCONTR runs after commit, but is asynchronous and hits the same ROLLBACK problem if it were a controlled operation
technical_details: BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CONFIRM_DEC with HEADER_CONTROL-POST_GI_FLG = 'X'
Unmanaged BO: read-only delivery list plus one instance action postGoodsIssue, no own persistence, no draft
Runtime error BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT, call chain LSC_ZI_PGI_CR=>SAVE -> BAPI -> SAPLV50I -> LV50IF01 ROLLBACK_CHECK
CALL FUNCTION ... DESTINATION 'NONE' with EXCEPTIONS system_failure, communication_failure, OTHERS, followed by BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT or BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK and RFC_CONNECTION_CLOSE
Pre-check objects: ENQUEUE_EVVBLKE, MARV (MM period), MARD and MCHB (unrestricted stock)
bgPF: cl_bgmc_process_factory, IF_BGMC_OP_SINGLE_TX_UNCONTR versus controlled operation via set_operation
Standard messages cited: M7 021 (stock deficit), delivery lock, missing CO account assignment (OKB9)
69.why_it_matters: It is a precise, real-world case of the conflict between legacy BAPIs that manage their own LUW and RAP's rule that the save phase must not roll back or commit. The three options show the trade-off between transactional consistency and a usable error message, which is the core design question for any RAP unmanaged BO that wraps a legacy BAPI.
69.developer_problem: How to call a legacy BAPI that issues ROLLBACK WORK on error from an unmanaged RAP BO for outbound delivery PGI without dumping in the save phase and without losing transactional consistency.
69.teaching_angle: Excellent case for an advanced RAP session. Walk through why ROLLBACK WORK is forbidden in the save phase (the RAP LUW owns commit and rollback), why determinations and the interaction phase differ, and what controlled versus uncontrolled bgPF operations guarantee. Ask trainees to propose a fourth option (for example, a wrapper that validates the BAPI result before save), then discuss its risks. The post itself gives no official answers to its four questions, so keep that gap visible in class.

deep_dives.title: BAPIs with ROLLBACK WORK inside a RAP unmanaged save
deep_dives.explanation:
In RAP the framework owns the LUW. In the save sequence (`finalize`, `check_before_save`, `adjust_numbers`, `save`) COMMIT WORK and ROLLBACK WORK are forbidden. A BAPI that reaches `ROLLBACK_CHECK` in `LV50IF01` and runs `ROLLBACK WORK` therefore raises `BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT`. This happens only on business-error paths, which is why the happy path looks fine.

The post's options: (A) call the BAPI via sRFC `DESTINATION 'NONE'` in the action handler (interaction phase), then `BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT` or `BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK`. This gives clean messages from the return table, but the commit is outside the RAP LUW. (B) keep the BAPI in `save` with pre-checks (`ENQUEUE_EVVBLKE`, MARV, MARD/MCHB). Unanticipated errors such as a missing OKB9 account assignment still dump. (C) `cl_bgmc_process_factory` with `IF_BGMC_OP_SINGLE_TX_UNCONTR` runs after commit in its own transaction, but it is asynchronous, and a controlled operation would hit the same ROLLBACK problem.

The trade-off is consistency against feedback. A is synchronous with real messages, but you must handle partial states, for example a BAPI success followed by a failure later in your own flow. C suits a case where the user can accept eventual status, with a status field and retry. The post gets no official answer, so test any choice for lock handling and failure recovery.

deep_dives.title: Rebuilding approval history from change documents
deep_dives.explanation:
EKKO and EBAN hold only the current release state (`FRGZU`). History lives in change documents: `CDHDR` (`objectclas`, `objectid`, `username`, `udate`, `utime`) joined to `CDPOS` (`tabname`, `fname = 'FRGZU'`, `value_new`). Object classes are `EINKBELEG` for PO/LTA and `BANF` for PR. The report derives the release level by counting 'X' in the new value, for example with `count( val = value_new sub = 'X' )`.

The UI is one `CL_SALV_TABLE`. Hotspot columns `DOCNO` and `SOURCE` are set with `if_salv_c_cell_type=>hotspot`, and a handler on `link_click` either drills down one level or pops a history stack. Helper columns stay in the table but are hidden with `set_visible( abap_false )`.

Pitfalls: `FOR ALL ENTRIES` returns everything if the driver table is empty, so guard it. Confirm change documents are written for the object. The excerpt is truncated and has typos, so test before reuse.

deep_dives.title: Choosing the right extension point per inbound channel
deep_dives.explanation:
The supplier invoice question shows a recurring Public Cloud problem. The same business object can be created via UI, EDI or A2A API, and each path may call different extension points. `LOG_EDI_MM_INVOICE_CE_MAP` targets B2B/EDI. The `MRM_*_DATA_MODIFY_CE` BAdIs (MRIS, MRDC, ERS) did not fire for the poster's tests, and the post does not say whether they were tested on the A2A path.

A practical method: confirm the channel, check the released BAdI list in ADT for that object, set a breakpoint or trace in the implementation, and run the exact channel. If none fires, the requirement may need a different mechanism, such as custom-field propagation through the API or a side-by-side approach. The post does not name the A2A API or the custom-field mechanism, so this is a method and not a solution.

interview_questions.question: Why does a BAPI that issues ROLLBACK WORK dump when called from the save method of an unmanaged RAP BO, and how would you handle it?
interview_questions.answer: In RAP the framework controls the LUW, and COMMIT WORK and ROLLBACK WORK are not allowed in the save sequence. A BAPI such as BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CONFIRM_DEC reaches ROLLBACK_CHECK in LV50IF01 on business errors and executes ROLLBACK WORK, which raises BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT. Options are to run the BAPI in a separate session via sRFC with DESTINATION 'NONE' in the action handler, with explicit BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT or ROLLBACK, or to run it after commit in a background process using bgPF. The sRFC route gives real messages but commits outside the RAP LUW. bgPF is asynchronous, so you need status and retry handling. Pre-checks reduce but cannot remove the risk of dumps.

interview_questions.question: How do you reconstruct who released a purchase order and when, since EKKO only holds the current status?
interview_questions.answer: Use change documents. Read CDHDR for objectclas EINKBELEG (PO, LTA) or BANF (PR) and the object ID, which gives username, udate and utime. Join CDPOS on the change number with fname FRGZU and the relevant tabname to get the new release value. The release level can be derived by counting 'X' in the new FRGZU value. Resolve full names from USER_ADDR. Check that change documents are actually written for the object, and when using FOR ALL ENTRIES, guard against an empty driver table because it would select all rows.

interview_questions.question: A team wants an LLM to query S/4HANA data through a custom MCP server. What architecture and security concerns would you raise?
interview_questions.answer: Direct SQL on HANA tables bypasses ABAP authority checks and CDS access control, so correct DB privileges do not give business-level authorization. It can also raise support and upgrade questions, which should be confirmed against current SAP statements. I would prefer released APIs, OData or CDS services with access control, exposed as narrowly scoped, predefined MCP tools rather than AI-generated SQL. Keep tools read-only where possible, log calls, and propagate the end user's identity instead of a technical user. Separate the three layers explicitly: database privilege, application authorization and the tool contract.
